extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/eligibility standards for filing and processing Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs) under 37 CFR 1.114, including what submissions qualify, timing, fee and form requirements, and examiner handling instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for filing an RCE / Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 37 CFR 1.114 apply to utility or plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or international applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995. The RCE provisions do not apply to: (A) a provisional application; (B) an application for a utility or plant patent filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) before June 8, 1995; (C) an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 before June 8, 1995; (D) an application for a design patent; or (E) a patent under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may obtain continued examination by filing an RCE (form PTO/SB/30), a submission, and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) prior to the earliest of: (A) payment of the issue fee (unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 is granted); (B) abandonment of the application; or (C) the filing of a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 or 146 (unless terminated). See 37 CFR 1.114(a) and (e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirement — what counts as a submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'submission' includes, but is not limited to, an information disclosure statement, an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reply to an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 is outstanding, the submission must meet the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111. A submission may consist of arguments in a previously filed appeal brief or reply brief, or incorporate them by reference. Previously filed after-final amendments (entered or unentered) may satisfy the submission requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement — filing prior to earliest event
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE and accompanying submission/fee must be filed prior to the earliest of payment of the issue fee, abandonment of the application, or filing of a notice of appeal/commencement of a civil action (unless terminated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the issue fee has been paid, a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw from issue must be granted to permit reopening; otherwise filing an RCE after the issue fee is paid will not avoid issuance of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission must include a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 to toll time
rubrics_metrics.description: The Submission: Must include a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 to the final rejection (e.g., an amendment filed with the RCE or a previously-filed after-final amendment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission that meets 1.111 is timely filed with the RCE and fee, the Office will withdraw the finality of any Office action to which a reply is outstanding and the submission will be entered and considered. Mere request and payment of the RCE fee will not toll the running of any time period set in the previous Office action for reply to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing verification items (TC checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical support personnel will verify that: (A) the RCE was filed on or after May 29, 2000; (B) the application was filed on or after June 8, 1995; (C) the application is a utility or plant application (not a design); (D) the application was pending when the RCE was filed; (E) prosecution in the application is closed (e.g., last Office action is final/notice of allowance/Quayle or the application is under appeal); (F) the RCE was filed before payment of the issue fee or a petition under 1.313 was filed and granted; (G) the RCE was accompanied by the proper fee(s) including 1.17(e); and (H) the RCE included a submission as required by 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one or more conditions are not satisfied, applicant will be so notified (generally Form PTO-2051). An improper RCE will not toll any time period set for reply and will not prevent abandonment if time expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot switch inventions / independent and distinct claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot file an RCE to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims that are independent and distinct from the claims previously claimed and examined as a matter of right (i.e., applicant cannot switch inventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any newly submitted claims directed to an invention independent and distinct from the previously claimed invention will be withdrawn from consideration and not entered. See 37 CFR 1.145 and MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous transmittal paper — CPA vs RCE treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a transmittal paper is ambiguous as to whether it is a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d) or an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114, the Office will: treat it as an RCE for plant/utility applications filed on/after June 8, 1995 (CPA practice eliminated), and treat it as a CPA for design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other papers filed with the transmittal (e.g., preliminary amendment or IDS) will not be taken into account in determining whether the transmittal is a CPA or RCE. If an unambiguous transmittal paper is an RCE filed in a design application, it will be treated as an improper RCE and Form PTO-2051 will be mailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE — notice and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more conditions for filing an RCE have not been satisfied, applicant will be notified (generally 'Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE),' Form PTO-2051).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An improper RCE will not operate to toll running of any time period set in the previous Office action for reply to avoid abandonment. If prosecution is not closed, applicant will be notified and any amendment/reply will be entered and forwarded for consideration under 37 CFR 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of conditional RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission is accompanied by a 'conditional' RCE and payment authorization (authorization to charge deposit account if submission would not otherwise be entered), the Office will treat the conditional RCE and payment as if an RCE and payment had been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This effectively treats the conditional payment as satisfying the fee requirement under 37 CFR 1.17(e) when the submission would otherwise be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and ordering of amendments filed with RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If the conditions for filing an RCE have been satisfied, previously filed unentered amendments and amendments filed with the RCE will normally be entered in the order filed unless specific instructions indicate otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant files conflicting or previously denied after-final amendments, applicant should clarify which amendments should be entered when filing the RCE. Applicants are encouraged to file all amendments no later than the filing of the RCE to avoid disapproval of entry under 37 CFR 1.111(b). If additional time is needed to prepare supplement, consider filing a suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(c) with the RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (manner of making amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any submission that is an amendment must comply with the manner of making amendments as set forth in 37 CFR 1.121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment must include markings showing the changes relative to the last entered amendment. Applicants are encouraged to file an amendment at the time of the RCE that incorporates all desired changes and to provide instructions regarding previously-filed unentered after-final amendments. Noncompliant amendments may prevent entry under 1.121.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not fully responsive submission — bona fide attempt requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If reply to a final Office action is outstanding and the submission is not fully responsive to the final Office action, then it must be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply to the final Office action in order for the RCE to toll the period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not a bona fide attempt, treat as improper RCE and mail Form PTO-2051. Examples of not bona fide: submission that only includes an IDS (IDS alone will not toll the period), or an amendment cancelling all claims and presenting no new/substitute claims. If bona fide but not fully responsive, mail notice, give shortened statutory period of one month or thirty days (whichever is longer) to complete the reply (see 37 CFR 1.135(c)) and use form paragraph 7.42.08.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant amendment that is bona fide
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE filed with a submission which is an amendment that is not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121, but which is a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply to the last Office action, should be treated as a proper RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mail 'Notice of Noncompliant Amendment' and give applicant one month or thirty days (whichever is longer) from mailing date to provide an amendment complying with 37 CFR 1.121 (see MPEP § 714.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of claims for different invention (nonelected invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed with an amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to a nonelected invention, the RCE should be treated as proper but the amendment should not be entered because it is not fully responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should be given one month or thirty days (whichever is longer) to submit a complete reply. Use form paragraphs 8.04 or 8.26 as appropriate. See 37 CFR 1.145 and MPEP § 821.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 132(a) provides that '[n]o amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of the invention.' Any amendment entered pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114 that is determined to contain new matter should be treated in the same manner that a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 determined to contain new matter is currently treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicant seeks to add new matter to the disclosure, the procedure in 37 CFR 1.114 is not available; the applicant must file a continuation-in-part (CIP) application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) containing such new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: First action after filing an RCE may be made final only if conditions met
rubrics_metrics.description: The action immediately subsequent to the filing of an RCE with a submission and fee under 37 CFR 1.114 may be made final only if the conditions set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It would not be proper to make final a first Office action immediately after the filing of an RCE if the first Office action includes a new ground of rejection. Use form paragraph 7.42.09 if appropriate to make the first action after filing the RCE final.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after allowance or Quayle action — reopening prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files an RCE with the fee and a submission in an application which has been allowed, prosecution will be reopened. However, if the issue fee has been paid, payment of the RCE fee and a submission without a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw from issue will not avoid issuance of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If RCE is filed in an allowed application prior to payment of the issue fee, a petition under 1.313 is not required. If filed after the issue fee has been paid and a petition under 1.313 is filed and granted, prosecution will be reopened but issue fee is not refundable; subsequent allowance will reflect the difference in issue fee due. Use form paragraph 7.42.05 to notify applicant that prosecution has been reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after appeal but before Board decision — withdrawal of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files an RCE after filing a Notice of Appeal to the Board but prior to a decision, it will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution before the examiner, regardless of whether the RCE is proper or improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will withdraw the appeal upon filing an RCE. Applicants should advise the Board when an RCE is filed in an application containing an appeal awaiting decision, otherwise the Board may refuse to vacate a decision rendered after the filing of the RCE. If the RCE is proper and includes a reply responsive under 37 CFR 1.111, withdraw finality and enter submission; if not fully responsive but bona fide, give time to complete reply (use form paragraph 7.42.06 and 7.42.08 as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA filed for utility/plant application treated as RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files a request for a CPA (on or after July 14, 2003) of a utility or plant application that was filed on or after June 8, 1995, the Office will automatically treat the improper CPA as an RCE of the prior application under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the CPA does not satisfy 1.114 requirements (e.g., lacks submission or fee), it will be treated as an improper RCE and the time period set in the last Office action will continue to run. If time has expired, applicant will need to file a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 to revive the application. The Office will not convert an improper CPA into an application under 1.53(b) except upon showing extenuating circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph use and examiner notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs are prescribed for examiner notification and correspondence regarding RCE processing (e.g., 7.42.04 withdraw finality after final rejection; 7.42.05 reopen after allowance; 7.42.06 after appeal; 7.42.08 not fully responsive; 7.42.09 first action final; 7.42.15 CPA treated as RCE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes accompany each form paragraph giving instructions on when to use them, what to insert in brackets (dates, reasons), and cross-references to applicable CFR and MPEP sections.
